children: Canada's Stellar AfricaGold has awarded a contract to Moroccan drilling contractor Compagnie Marocaine des Forages Minier (CMFM) for Phase II diamond drilling at the Tichka Est Gold Project in Morocco, the company announced on Tuesday.
The fully funded programme comprises 24 diamond drill holes totalling approximately 5,000 metres.
The company, which is listed TSX Venture Exchange (TSXV), said rig mobilisation has commenced, with drilling expected to start in October 2026.
The contract was awarded following a competitive tender process. Stellar AfricaGold did not disclose the financial value of the contract.
Tichka Est comprises five research permits and one exploitation licence covering 82 square kilometres in Morocco's High Atlas region, approximately 90km south of Marrakech.

Under an earn-in agreement with Morocco's Office National des Hydrocarbures et des Mines (ONHYM), Stellar can earn an 85 percent interest in the project by incurring $2.39 million in exploration expenditure over three years.
Gold mineralisation has been identified in three areas — Zones A, B and C — with Zone B representing the most advanced area following recent drilling, according to the company.

Separately, Stellar AfricaGold has signed a contract with geophysical contractor PROGREM SARL for a high-resolution, closely spaced drone magnetic survey covering Zones A, B and C. Data acquisition is scheduled for October 2026.
(Writing by Majda Muhsen; Editing by Anoop Menon)
